title: build-pipeline
description: Learn about build-pipeline. Master the concepts, patterns, and best practices.

data.text: Build pipelines automate the process of converting source code into production-ready assets. A well-optimized build pipeline includes transpilation, bundling, optimization, testing, and deployment, ensuring consistent, high-quality builds.
Modern build pipelines typically include: source code checkout, dependency installation, linting, testing, transpilation, bundling, optimization, artifact generation, and deployment.

data.title: Build Pipeline Architecture
data.content: Typical stages in a modern build pipeline.
data.code:
Build Pipeline Stages:

1. Source Code Checkout
   - Clone repository
   - Checkout specific branch/commit
   - Fetch submodules

2. Dependency Installation
   - Install node_modules
   - Install system dependencies
   - Cache dependencies for speed

3. Code Quality Checks
   - Linting (ESLint, Stylelint)
   - Type checking (TypeScript)
   - Format checking (Prettier)
   - Security scanning

4. Testing
   - Unit tests
   - Integration tests
   - E2E tests
   - Code coverage

5. Transpilation
   - TypeScript to JavaScript
   - JSX to JavaScript
   - SCSS to CSS
   - Asset optimization

6. Bundling
   - Module resolution
   - Code splitting
   - Tree shaking
   - Dependency bundling

7. Optimization
   - Minification
   - Compression
   - Image optimization
   - Asset hashing

8. Artifact Generation
   - Source maps
   - Build reports
   - Bundle analysis

9. Deployment
   - Upload to CDN
   - Deploy to servers
   - Cache invalidation
   - Health checks

data.text: Execute independent build stages in parallel to reduce total build time. Use dependency graphs to identify which stages can run concurrently.

data.title: Parallel Build Stages
data.code:
# .github/workflows/optimized-build.yml
name: Optimized Build
on: [push]
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v2
      
      # Install dependencies once
      - name: Install Dependencies
        run: npm ci
      
      # Run independent tasks in parallel
      - name: Lint & Type Check
        run: npm run lint && npm run typecheck
      
      - name: Unit Tests
        run: npm run test:unit
      
      - name: Integration Tests
        run: npm run test:integration
      
      # Dependent tasks run after
      - name: Build
        run: npm run build
        needs: [lint-and-type-check, unit-tests, integration-tests]
      
      - name: E2E Tests
        run: npm run test:e2e
        needs: [build]

# Time savings:
# Sequential: 15 minutes
# Parallel: 8 minutes

data.text: Only rebuild what has changed since the last build. Use file hashing, intelligent caching, and incremental compilation to speed up builds.

data.title: Incremental Build Strategy
data.content: Implement incremental builds for faster iterations.

data.text: Generate meaningful build artifacts including source maps, build reports, and bundle analysis. These artifacts help with debugging and performance monitoring.

data.title: Build Artifact Generation

data.text: Implement quality gates that prevent broken builds from reaching production. Include linting, testing, performance budgets, and security checks.

data.title: Quality Gate Configuration
data.content: Enforce quality standards in build pipeline.

data.text: Monitor build pipeline performance and success rates. Track metrics like build duration, cache hit rates, and failure reasons to identify optimization opportunities.

data.title: Build Pipeline Metrics
Build Pipeline Complexity
data.text: Avoid over-engineering build pipelines. Start simple, add complexity only when needed. Complex pipelines are harder to debug and maintain.

terms.definition: Automated process that converts source code into production-ready assets through multiple stages.
Building only the parts of the application that have changed since the last build.
Automated checks that prevent broken or non-compliant code from advancing through the pipeline.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Build pipelines automate code transformation into production assets
Typical stages: checkout, dependencies, quality checks, testing, transpilation, bundling, optimization, deployment
Use parallel processing for independent build stages to reduce total time
Implement incremental builds to only rebuild changed code
Generate meaningful artifacts: source maps, build reports, bundle analysis
Set up quality gates: linting, testing, performance budgets, security checks
Monitor pipeline performance and success rates for optimization
data.takeaway: An optimized build pipeline is essential for consistent, high-quality software delivery, enabling fast iteration while maintaining quality standards.
